title: Assertion–Reason
description: Judge the assertion, the reason, and whether the reason explains the assertion.
instructions: Every question in this quiz is of one type: Assertion–Reason.
Use it to test how this question type looks and is marked.

questions.assertion: A voltmeter is connected in parallel with the component being measured.
questions.reason: A voltmeter has a very high resistance, so it draws almost no current.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the reason explains why. (Answer A)
Both are true, but shininess does not explain conduction. (Answer B)

questions.assertion: The pH of pure water at 25 °C is 7.
questions.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: water ionises slightly. (Answer C)

questions.assertion: A binary search can be used on any list.
questions.reason: Binary search repeatedly halves the search space.
questions.explanation: The assertion is false because the list must be sorted. The reason is true. (Answer D)

questions.reason: Hydrogen has a full outer shell of eight electrons.
questions.explanation: Both are false: hydrogen has one electron and is not a noble gas. (Answer E)
